attacks.claim: The public patch-note copy says local saves stay put, but on launch the game downloads and replaces the local slot whenever the cloud copy is newer and the local slot is older. Patch notes shipped to 182k players therefore misdescribe what Cross-Save does.
attacks.evidence: Patch notes: 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are.' vs. 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.'

attacks.claim: Newest-copy and conflict detection depend on last-modified timestamps from different PCs. The artifact does not say whether these are client or server times, how 'changed since last sync' is computed, or whether skew is tolerated. A skewed clock could make an older save look newer and replace the newer one.
attacks.evidence: 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.' / 'If both changed since last sync, the game asks' — ABSENT: clock source, skew tolerance, and how 'changed since last sync' is determined

attacks.claim: The 1.3 round-trip is not validated. 1.3 ignores sync.meta, so a 1.3 session can leave metadata stale, and the artifact does not show that 1.3 preserves the new modifier keys when it re-saves. QA only checked that 1.4 saves load in 1.3, not that a 1.3 session followed by a 1.4 sync keeps progress. This bears directly on the agreed 'never lose a save' rule.
attacks.evidence: '1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save.' / QA: 'Downgrade to 1.3 ... Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored' (no re-save then 1.4 sync check)

attacks.claim: No compare-and-set or base-version check on upload is described. With four PCs syncing the same slot, concurrent uploads can race, and the last write wins silently.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: upload concurrency control or base-version check; the security section covers auth and rate limits, not write ordering

attacks.claim: The server never parses or validates blobs and keeps only 5 versions per slot. A 1.4 build that writes bad saves would push out every good server copy within five uploads, so loss protection then depends only on the 3 local backups.
attacks.evidence: 'the server never parses them' and 'the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally'

attacks.claim: The Epic production path is essentially unverified. QA ran on an Epic dev sandbox build, the beta had only 150 sandbox testers, and EOS sandbox accounts and tokens differ from production. The cabined restriction and linking are therefore unproven on real accounts, yet Epic is 29% of players.
attacks.evidence: 'Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox' and 'Epic sandbox testers (150)'

attacks.claim: QA ran on a private Steam branch and a sandbox Epic build, and the downgrade test ran only on the Steam beta branch. Rollback restores 1.3 on both stores. The signed production builds and store configuration that ship on Dec 2 are not shown to behave the same way.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam build 18204411 on a private branch' / 'Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch 1.3-legacy)' / '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores'

attacks.claim: The rollout justification cites beta results (0 lost saves, 11 conflict prompts) for 18-30 November, but the artifact is dated 2026-10-26, so those results cannot exist yet. The 'never lose a save' justification for the Dec 2 launch rests on them.
attacks.evidence: '1. Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch ... 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players.'

attacks.claim: Retention and deletion of the persistent steam_id to epic_account_id link are not stated. Backend request logs (which contain IPs and IDs) have no stated retention. The 24-month inactivity rule covers only save data. Links also have no deletion trigger on store-account closure or on uninstall.
attacks.evidence: 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted' covers save data only; ABSENT: link retention, log retention, and deletion trigger on account closure

attacks.claim: The privacy disclosure appears inaccurate. sync.meta includes a device name, which is often personal, yet the artifact states no name data is stored and bases the updated privacy policy on that statement.
attacks.evidence: sync.meta fields 'slot, playtime, last-modified, device name' vs. 'No email, name, payment or friends data.'

attacks.claim: Cabined (under-13) accounts are addressed only for linking. The artifact does not say whether their save blobs or sync.meta are uploaded or whether any data is collected from them, which is where minor-protection rules apply.
attacks.evidence: 'for them linking is not offered and the screen explains why.' ABSENT: whether cabined players' save and sync.meta data is uploaded or stored

attacks.claim: The kill switch and the automatic budget stop are rollback and safety controls, but neither appears in the QA table. The kill switch is read only on launch and every 10 minutes, so its behaviour is untested.
attacks.evidence: 'at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically' and 'Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false' — ABSENT: QA result for either

attacks.claim: The load test covers 30k concurrent launches over 10 minutes, but the release is a same-moment 10:00 PT push to all 182k players on both stores. That synchronized spike, plus retries on 503 and the 60 uploads/hour cap, is not shown to be covered by the test.
attacks.evidence: 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores' and 'Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors'

attacks.claim: Conflict-prompt handling is unspecified when the player dismisses the prompt, the game crashes during it, or the launch is offline while a conflict is pending. The artifact does not say whether the slot stays unsynced indefinitely or can be overwritten on a later launch.
attacks.evidence: 'Nothing is overwritten without that choice.' — ABSENT: behaviour for dismissed, interrupted, or unanswered prompts

attacks.claim: 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' deletes all server copies within 24 h, and the artifact mentions no confirmation step or recovery window for that deletion.
attacks.evidence: 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' removes the link and all server copies within 24 h'

attacks.claim: The 24-month purge is not stopped by the kill switch, so cloud data can be deleted while sync is disabled. The artifact does not address this.
attacks.evidence: 'Server copies and links are kept so sync resumes when re-enabled.' vs. 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted'

attacks.claim: The 140 GB storage forecast is not shown to follow from the stated per-slot size and retention, and its assumptions (slots used, versions retained, opt-in count) are not given.
attacks.evidence: '~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month'

attacks.claim: Upload timing is undefined. Sync is described only at launch, so changes made on one PC and then played on another without a clean exit may not reach the cloud, and conflict behaviour in that window is not specified.
attacks.evidence: 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy' — ABSENT: when uploads happen (exit, periodic, after save)

attacks.claim: A cloud blob that fails the checksum is not loaded and the previous version is kept, but the artifact does not say what the next sync does with it. The corrupt blob could stay the newest server version and cause repeated downloads or a conflict loop.
attacks.evidence: 'a blob that fails is not loaded, the previous version is kept'

attacks.claim: 'Every replaced version is kept' conflicts with the 5-version server limit and the 3-version local limit, so older replaced versions are deleted.
attacks.evidence: 'Every replaced version is kept: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally'

attacks.claim: Monitoring has no signal for data-loss precursors such as checksum or schema rejections, conflict-prompt backup choices, cross-store link failures, or failed unlink deletions. A silent divergence bug would surface only through player reports.
attacks.evidence: 'Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate.'

attacks.claim: Conflict-prompt timestamps have no timezone or source device, so a player comparing devices across time zones may choose the wrong save.
attacks.evidence: 'Keep the save on this PC (12 h 41 m, today 18:02) or the cloud save (13 h 05 m, today 21:40)?'

attacks.claim: No recovery path is described when a player can no longer sign in to one store (lost or banned account). The only remedy stated, 'unlink first', requires access to both stores.
attacks.evidence: 'Each store account can be in at most one link.' / 'Refused with unlink first message'

attacks.claim: Localization of the new prompts, error text, and the title-screen status line is not addressed, and it is unclear whether the status line is exposed to screen readers.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: localization or screen-reader coverage for 'Cross-Save: synced 2 min ago' and the error string; only 'screen narration for the conflict prompt' is listed

attacks.claim: No data export mechanism is described for players to retrieve their cloud saves or links, which limits data-portability compliance.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players.' — ABSENT: data export for cloud saves
